paper.title: Mock Paper · Primary 3 Language Use and Comprehension (A)
paper.note: The first of three Primary 3 papers. A school-exam paper, not a PSLE paper: shorter, and with no synthesis section. Sit it in one go with a timer, then go through the mistakes before sitting the next one.

questions.q: My brother and I ______ to the library every Saturday.
There ______ three cats under the car.
Priya ______ her water bottle at home yesterday.
The kittens drank all of ______ milk.
Put the umbrella ______ the door, please.
______ you like some more rice?
He ran quickly ______ he still missed the bus.
This is the ______ mango I have ever eaten.
My grandmother ______ in Malacca for forty years.
Nobody ______ where the key is.

sections.name: Booklet B · Grammar Cloze
sections.instruction: Fill each blank with one suitable word.
sections.passage:
Last Saturday my class visited a farm in Kranji.

We left school at eight o'clock (1)______ bus, and the journey took almost an hour. Mrs Ong counted us twice (2)______ we got off.

The farmer, Mr Samad, (3)______ waiting for us at the gate. He showed us rows (4)______ green vegetables growing under long white nets. The nets, he explained, keep the insects (5)______.

Each of us (6)______ given a small pot and three seeds to plant. Mine is on my windowsill now, (7)______ it has not grown at all.

It was the best school trip I (8)______ ever been on.

answers.tip: 'By bus' is the set phrase for how you travel.
Either works: she counted them before or after they got off.
'Mr Samad' is singular and the story is in the past.
'Rows of vegetables' is the set phrase.
'Keep the insects out' means stop them getting in.
'Each of us' is singular, and this is the passive: was given.
The two ideas disagree, so 'but' is needed.
'Have ever been on' after 'the best … I'.

sections.name: Booklet B · Spelling and Grammar Editing
sections.instruction: There is one spelling or grammar error in each numbered line. Write the correction — one word only.

questions.q: Every morning my mother wake me up at half past six.
questions.tip: The error was “wake”. 'My mother' is singular.

questions.q: I brush my teeths and wash my face before breakfast.
questions.tip: The error was “teeths”. The plural of 'tooth' is 'teeth'.

questions.q: My favourite breakfast are bee hoon with an egg.
questions.tip: The error was “are”. 'My favourite breakfast' is singular.

questions.q: We walk to school togather because it is very near.
questions.tip: The error was “togather”. It is spelt to-geth-er.

questions.q: Yesterday it rain very heavily on the way there.
questions.tip: The error was “rain”. 'Yesterday' needs the past tense.

questions.q: My sister forgot to bring she umbrella.
questions.tip: The error was “she”. A possessive is needed before 'umbrella'.

questions.q: She was very wet when we arrive at the gate.
questions.tip: The error was “arrive”. It must match the past tense of 'was'.

questions.q: The teacher gave her a dry towle from the cupboard.
questions.tip: The error was “towle”. It is spelt t-o-w-e-l.

questions.q: There was many puddles in the car park that day.
Now I always keep a umbrella in my bag.
questions.tip: The error was “a”. 'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound.

sections.name: Booklet B · Comprehension
sections.instruction: Read the passage and answer the questions. Note the marks for each question.
sections.passage:
The Mango Tree

There is a mango tree behind our block. It is older than my father.

Every year, in April, it makes far more mangoes than one family could eat. Most of them fall onto the grass and spoil, because nobody can reach the high branches.

Last April, my grandfather had an idea. He tied an old plastic bottle to the end of a long bamboo pole. He cut the bottom off the bottle first, so that a mango would drop straight into it.

It worked. In one afternoon we picked forty-one mangoes.

That was far too many for us. My grandfather washed them, put them into paper bags, and wrote a number on each bag. Then he gave one bag to every flat on our floor. There are eight flats, so each bag had five mangoes in it, and one was left over for him.

The next morning, somebody had left a tin of biscuits outside our door. There was no note.

A week later, Mrs Rahim from the flat at the end knocked and gave us a jar of mango chutney she had made from her bag. She said she had not spoken to anybody on our floor for two years.

The tree is still there. My grandfather still has the bamboo pole behind the door, and he keeps the bottle on it all year, even in the months when there is nothing at all to pick.

questions.q: Where is the mango tree?
questions.a: It is behind their block of flats.

questions.q: Why did most of the mangoes spoil before the grandfather's idea?
questions.a: They fell onto the grass and were wasted, because nobody could reach the high branches to pick them.

questions.q: Describe the tool the grandfather made.
questions.a: He tied an old plastic bottle to the end of a long bamboo pole, and cut the bottom off the bottle so that a mango would drop straight into it.

questions.q: How many mangoes did they pick in one afternoon?
How do we know the grandfather wanted to be fair to the neighbours?
questions.a: He gave a bag to every flat on the floor, put the same number of mangoes in each bag, and kept only the one that was left over for himself.

questions.q: Who do you think left the tin of biscuits, and why is the writer not certain?
questions.a: It was probably one of the neighbours who had been given a bag of mangoes. The writer cannot be certain because there was no note with the tin.

questions.q: What did Mrs Rahim do with her mangoes, and what did she tell the family when she came?
questions.a: She made mango chutney from them and brought a jar of it to the family. She told them she had not spoken to anybody on their floor for two years.

questions.q: How do we know the neighbours were grateful? Give one piece of evidence.
questions.a: Either: somebody left a tin of biscuits outside their door the next morning; or Mrs Rahim brought them a jar of mango chutney a week later.

questions.q: Which word in the passage means 'go bad'?
questions.tip: Look in the paragraph about the mangoes that fell onto the grass.

questions.q: What does the grandfather hope will happen next April, and how do we know?
questions.a: He hopes there will be another crop of mangoes to pick and share. We know because he keeps the bottle on the bamboo pole all year round, ready, even in the months when there is nothing to pick.

questions.q: Why do you think the grandfather wrote a number on each paper bag?
questions.a: So that he could make sure every bag held the same number of mangoes and every flat got a fair share. It shows he had counted them and wanted to divide them evenly.
questions.tip: Think about why counting would matter when you are giving something to eight different flats.
